head: 05d151914cab2f8b1f09dee95f5972e8080d6f4d
summary:
The slice's only deliverable is `.taad/fitness.yaml`, committed on slice/SL-022 in 05d1519 as blob 3c47d3b. Nothing under src/ or tests/ changed. The Fitness MCP tool, which is what validate uses, ran in this slice's own worktree and gave '8 rule(s) checked against 33 file(s) read. Every declared rule holds.' It gave that text both before and after a full build, with no MATCHED NO FILES section. op=rules lists all 8 rooted entries with \b and \s intact. That closes C4 on this record, and C1 and C2 with it. The C3 effect was checked by calling the engine's own `_append_rules`, which is committed at taad_v3 HEAD 0260e7e. It added a 9th rule, left the original 6814 bytes as an unchanged prefix, and the check still passed.

I ran my own plants in a scratch copy under %TEMP%, separate from the builder's. There were 13 planted violations across all 8 entries:
- a using directive at Scanner.cs:7
- a DllImport in a // comment, in src and in tests
- UseWPF and a ProjectReference to App in the Core .csproj
- IsReparsePoint in a .xaml
- FileAttributes.ReparsePoint and 0x00000400 in MainWindow.xaml.cs
- Skip=, Explicit=true and SkipException in CancellationTests.cs
- Directory.EnumerateFiles in Scanner.cs
- 0x400 in Native/LongPath.cs

Every one fired on the expected entry and at the same file:line that xUnit reported, on the same tree. Tokens planted in the exempted Kernel32.cs, EntryClassifier.cs and TestNative.cs fired in neither engine. For all five Facts, the files each entry covers are exactly the files xUnit's Files() reads.

A built copy passed with 33 files read and no violations. It held WPF App.g.cs and MainWindow.g.cs, LibraryImports.g.cs, and violation files planted in .dotnet/, artifacts/, TestResults/, bin/ and obj/. The controls behaved as expected:
- A typo'd glob is reported as unmatched.
- A tree with no yaml reads NONE.
- A `$`-anchored probe rule fires on a CRLF file.

The full suite passes 86/86.

Two things keep this from passing outright:
1. **O-007 is not fixed.** It is a minor fix owed to build-slice, and the yaml still has the unfixed pattern. When I planted a UTF-8 BOM file with `using System.Windows;` on line 1, xUnit failed it at :1 and Fitness passed it. So the header's claim at lines 13-15, 'Both fail on the same files', is still false.
2. **Criterion 13 is not met, as the design predicted.** A slice cut before this merges reads NONE. The design marked this non-material.

There is no loop: each stage made one attempt.

checks.what: Fitness MCP op=check again after the full suite rebuilt the worktree
checks.evidence: Identical text: 8 rules, 33 files, every declared rule holds.

checks.what: Fitness MCP op=rules: the file loads and lists every rooted entry
checks.evidence: '8 rule(s) in .taad\fitness.yaml'. Every entry is rooted at src/ or tests/, patterns show (?m) with \b and \s intact (e.g. /(?m)0x0*400\b/), and except_files are listed.

checks.what: Deliverable scope: what the slice actually changed
checks.evidence: Only .taad/fitness.yaml (+120) plus the engine's own .taad/slices/SL-022 records. No src/ or tests/ change. The yaml has no uncommitted edits.

checks.what: O-001: every yaml pattern equals its xUnit verbatim literal plus a leading (?m)
checks.command: python %TEMP%\sl022-val\o001_o004.py (parses ArchitectureRulesTests.cs @"..." literals and the yaml via PyYAML)
checks.evidence: 8/8 entries equal, 0 differing (4/4/4/4/5/5/1/1 patterns). xUnit uses only RegexOptions.Multiline (ArchitectureRulesTests.cs:85), no pattern has `$`, and there are 0 double-quoted scalars in the rules body. All entries have including_comments=True.

checks.what: Clean scratch copy (git ls-files of the worktree) through the engine's fitness.check
checks.command: taad3.fitness.check(%TEMP%\sl022-val\clean) from taad_v3 backend at HEAD 0260e7e, shared venv Python 3.13.14, PyYAML 6.0.3
checks.evidence: verdict pass, 8 rules, content_files 33, unmatched [], unran [], 0 hits. render(): '8 rule(s) checked against 33 file(s) read. Every declared rule holds.', the same text as the MCP tool on the worktree.

checks.what: xUnit ArchitectureRulesTests on the planted copy (13 planted violations, plus exempt-file tokens, plus a BOM file)
checks.evidence: Failed 5/5 as intended, exit 1. The trx lists 14 (Fact, file, line) hits: the 13 planned plus PlantedBom.cs:1.

checks.what: Fitness on the same planted copy: does each plant fire on the right entry at the same file:line as xUnit? (cases 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 12)

The hits cover: Scanner.cs:7 using (after a non-blank line), a comment DllImport at Scanner.cs:9 and a LibraryImport at CancellationTests.cs:14, UseWPF at Core.csproj:8 and a ProjectReference at :9, IsReparsePoint at MainWindow.xaml:8, the reparse flag and 0x00000400 at MainWindow.xaml.cs:12-13, Skip/Explicit/SkipException at CancellationTests.cs:8/10/13, EnumerateFiles at Scanner.cs:11, and 0x400 at LongPath.cs:85. Tokens appended to Kernel32.cs, EntryClassifier.cs and TestNative.cs fired in neither engine.

checks.what: O-006 / case 2: the file is not gitignored and is tracked
checks.evidence: check-ignore exit 1 with no output. The file is tracked as 100644 3c47d3bd4ac2..., last changed in 05d1519.

checks.evidence: Passed 86, Failed 0, Skipped 0, exit 0. git status afterwards shows only the engine's SL-022 records.

criteria.criterion: 1. Fitness loads the rule file at validate (committed on the slice branch, \b and \s patterns single-quoted)
criteria.how: The Fitness MCP tool in this worktree: op=rules lists 8 entries with \b and \s intact, and op=check says '8 rule(s) checked against 33 file(s) read. Every declared rule holds.' The file is committed in 05d1519. There are 0 double-quoted scalars.

criteria.criterion: 2. The file reaches trunk (not matched by .gitignore)
criteria.how: git check-ignore exit 1 on .taad/fitness.yaml and .taad/, and the file is tracked on the branch. Actually reaching trunk happens at merge, after validate (see not_reached).

criteria.criterion: 3. The screen-free rule fires on a using directive after line 1 (Scanner.cs:7)
criteria.how: In the planted scratch copy, Fitness reported 'TheScannerCoreDoesNotKnowAboutTheScreen (*.cs)' at Scanner.cs:7 and xUnit reported the same file:line.

criteria.criterion: 4. The interop rule fires on a token inside a // comment
criteria.how: '// planted: DllImport belongs in Native' fired InteropLivesOnlyInNative (src) at Scanner.cs:9. '// planted: LibraryImport' fired (tests) at CancellationTests.cs:14. In both, Fitness and xUnit gave the same line and in_comments was empty.

criteria.criterion: 5. A rule spanning two file types fires in the second type only
criteria.how: UseWPF and a ProjectReference to App in Core.csproj fired the (*.csproj) entry at :8 and :9. IsReparsePoint in MainWindow.xaml fired the (*.xaml) entry at :8. Both matched xUnit.

criteria.criterion: 6. The widened reparse rule fires outside the classifier (App project)
criteria.how: FileAttributes.ReparsePoint and 0x00000400 in MainWindow.xaml.cs fired at :12 and :13 in both engines. 0x400 in Native/LongPath.cs also fired, which shows the reparse exemption is exact to Kernel32.cs.

criteria.criterion: 7. Exempted files may hold the token (Kernel32.cs, EntryClassifier.cs, TestNative.cs)
criteria.how: The clean tree passes, and extra tokens appended to all three files fired in neither Fitness nor xUnit.

criteria.criterion: 8. The tests/**/*.cs entries run over ArchitectureRulesTests.cs without failing on its own literals
criteria.how: The clean worktree and the clean copy pass with including_comments true on every entry. The (*.cs) and (tests) entries cover 16 and 15 test files, and ArchitectureRulesTests.cs is among them.

criteria.criterion: 9. The rooted globs cover their target files (no glob matches nothing)
criteria.how: MCP op=check has no MATCHED NO FILES section and the engine's Report.unmatched is []. Per-Fact covered sets are exactly xUnit's Files() sets (13/14/7/16/27). A typo control shows an unmatched glob is reported.

criteria.criterion: 10. op=check on a built worktree gives the clean verdict
criteria.how: A scratch copy was built with EmitCompilerGeneratedFiles (App.g.cs, MainWindow.g.cs, LibraryImports.g.cs), with violation files planted in .dotnet/, artifacts/, TestResults/, bin/ and obj/. It passed: 8 rules, 33 files. The MCP check on the real worktree with .dotnet/ and bin/obj also passed.

criteria.criterion: 11. A `$`-anchored pattern matches on a CRLF checkout
criteria.how: The shipped file has no `$` pattern, so this is vacuous for the deliverable. A probe rule ending in `$` fired at Scanner.cs:7 on a CRLF file.

criteria.criterion: 12. The never-skipped rule fires on a skipped counting test
criteria.how: [Fact(Skip = ...)], [Fact(Explicit = true)] and SkipException in CancellationTests.cs fired at :8, :10 and :13 in both engines.

criteria.criterion: 13. A slice cut before this merges reads the rules
criteria.how: A tree without .taad/fitness.yaml reads NONE. The design (material: false) predicted this as a known limit. Q-010 handles it by cutting later slices after the merge or rebasing them onto it.

criteria.criterion: 14. A later design appends its declared rules onto the hand-written file
criteria.how: The committed taad3.design._append_rules (HEAD 0260e7e) added a 9th rule. The original bytes are an unchanged prefix, the first 8 rules are identical and check still passes. This was measured by a direct call, not through a real design stage.

obligations.evidence: A script diff of all 8 entries against the ArchitectureRulesTests.cs @"..." literals found 0 entries differing, each equal to the literal plus a leading (?m). The only RegexOptions is Multiline (line 85) and no `$` anchor exists. The planted runs showed the same hit sets in both engines.
The MCP op=check report has no MATCHED NO FILES section. The engine's Report.unmatched is [] on the clean and built copies. The typo control shows a non-matching glob does get listed.
yaml.safe_load top-level keys are ['rules'] with 8 entries. MCP op=rules parses all 8. The committed _append_rules extended it to 9 loadable rules.
On a scratch copy, _append_rules kept the original 6814 bytes as an exact prefix. The first 8 loaded rules are identical before and after, and check passes with 9 rules on 33 files and 0 unmatched.
git grep at taad_v3 HEAD 0260e7e finds def _append_rules at backend/taad3/design.py:1037. git status shows only backend/tests files modified, so design.py matches the commit.
git check-ignore -v .taad/fitness.yaml .taad/ exits 1 with no match. git ls-files -s lists the blob 3c47d3b as tracked.

This obligation is owed to build-slice and has not been discharged. yaml lines 37/47 still read '(?m)^\s*using...' with no optional U+FEFF, and header lines 13-15 still claim both engines fail on the same files. Re-measured: a BOM file with `using System.Windows;` on line 1 fails xUnit at PlantedBom.cs:1 and passes Fitness. It is minor, because no file in the tree has a BOM and xUnit remains the backstop, but it stands.

not_reached: The file has not reached trunk yet. The merge, and a later slice cut after it reading 8 rules at its own validate, were not observed.
A real later design stage with non-empty architecture_rules writing into this file. Only _append_rules was called directly on a scratch copy.

The Fitness MCP tool reads only this worktree, so all planted-violation shapes ran through the engine's fitness module in-process on %TEMP% copies. It is the same module, and the clean-tree text is identical to the MCP output, but the plants were never seen through the MCP path itself.
The real worktree's App project had no WPF *.g.cs, because the suite does not build App there. Generated-source coverage comes from the scratch built copy only.
Multi-line constructs, where Fitness matches across line breaks and xUnit does not, and UTF-16 source files were not planted.

Whether the engine's own gating logic treats a report with a non-empty unmatched list as not-clean. The typo control returned verdict 'pass' with unmatched populated. Report.clean covers it, but how validate or code-review gates read it was not observed.
